answer.answer: Audit confirms the ZIP import is complete, losslessly retained, reconciled without creating another canonical snapshot, and bounded so rejected Flowworks analysis remains historical only.

claims.value: `Star Rupture Game Analysis.zip`, supplied 2026-07-11, was preserved with its verified extracted tree under ignored `imports/star-rupture-game-analysis__20260708T190137Z/raw/`. The ZIP is 21,674,717 bytes with SHA-256 `1a1c1ef0ae00905ced37f1221ab22c4b9268f2ebe17b7516e6c9cac67d7f6fa3`; it has 123 entries including directories and 115 manifested files plus `CHECKSUMS.sha256`. `unzip -t` and every packaged SHA-256 passed. Tracked `MANIFEST.csv` and `CHECKSUMS.sha256` provide the audit ledger while the duplicate third-party corpus, personalized save context, generated binaries, and legacy SQLite database remain local and Git-ignored. The archive data retrieval time is `2026-07-08T19:01:37Z`, and the import was recorded at `2026-07-11T19:54:52Z`.

The archive’s repeated `23761620` numeric-data label is corrected to a two-axis boundary: numerical source data belongs to Update 1 internal game version `35118973`, dated `2026-04-09`, contextually mapped—not directly equated by SRDB—to Steam build `22674441` and inferred semantic version `0.2.0`. The immutable source capture is SRDB `2.3.4`, snapshot `ea-u1-gv35118973__srdb-2.3.4__20260711T050230Z`, captured at `2026-07-11T05:02:30.009644Z`. Separately, the latest public executable observed was Hotfix `0.2.8`, Steam build `23761620`, released `2026-06-17`. The archive’s source-site version and reliable per-value game-build provenance were not recorded, so its legacy calculations retain their July 8 boundary and must not receive the canonical snapshot ID until actually ported and rerun.

No second canonical game-data snapshot was installed. Reconciliation found complete overlap for 468 items, 191 public buildings, 234 recipe definitions, 6 corporations/77 levels, 121 export offers, 15 development upgrades, 3,259 map markers, and 3,094 loot entries; the official-news subset was also duplicated by the richer canonical corpus. The promoted distinct evidence was: player model `rourke-update1-save-baseline__20260711`; six medium-confidence Ore Excavator v2 links for Calcium, Titanium, and Wolfram Impure/Pure recipes to `mechanical-drill-tier2`; 15 medium-confidence consumable calorie/hydration assumptions kept separate from raw item records with an explicit verification warning; nine site/geography assets (`faraday-works-map.png`, `flowworks-proposed-site.png`, `grand-basin-build-pad.png`, `grand-basin-region.png`, `landerworks-map.png`, `world-map-central-corridor.png`, `world-map-named-sites.png`, `world-map-named-sites.svg`, and `world-map-overview.png`); and consolidated player-save, architecture, geography, progression, exploration, food, and remote-resource notes. The comparison also corrected the `airlock` item/building collision and normalized Training Corporation’s literal `$undefined` sentinel to null. Legacy reports/models remain verified raw-import evidence until recomputed.

All 18 `Flowworks Campaign Sizing - Levels 8 to 15` artifacts are `superseded_audit_only`: they remain in the verified raw import for historical audit but cannot become current guidance. The rejected model overemphasized output storage and led toward a three-Stabilizer/two-slow-press design. Current authority is the July 11 staged plan in `Player save - progression and next builds.md`, which is adopted planning—not confirmed construction. Its level-10 cell uses one Stabilizer, one Nozzle, one Impeller, two Valves, one Turbine, and two Pumps; the second Stabilizer is added only before Scanner/levels 11–12, while one HRS v2 pad is merely reserved and built only if imported-HRS recovery fails in practice. Current installed truth remains the sites/freight note, while the progression note governs plans; whether Flowworks construction has begun remains unresolved.

answer.answer: The three dumps are preserved losslessly as provenance, deduplicated into one historical record, and separated from current installed state, recommendations, questions, and unbuilt plans.

claims.value: Dump 01 is a formatting variant of the prior factory-planning export: lines 1-226 reproduce that sequence and add no unique conversation content. Dump 02 overlaps through lines 1-96 and contributes unique scaling/product-history material at lines 99-249. Dump 03 overlaps at lines 2-91, repeats the final export request at line 229, and contributes unique exploration/combat material at lines 95-225. The preserved source hashes are respectively a6534f50df6a09c98d6e3465488b60a60e5452a47cc2f63251df049c1cdc4be1, adde9855a1c3e439a02b6ccb243779ab29ed6a40602d15316caa369e1d90ec6d, and dc259be82ef89c908785b59644fa1f27f2be914c43f95f4f35351f94e1803a40.

Only direct first-person reports may establish player state, history, preferences, or observations. Questions establish goals or uncertainty, not their premises; quoted assistant text is not an independent player observation; recommendations do not establish ownership; and accepted or selected plans remain distinct from installed/completed state. Durable state must retain classifications such as confirmed_current, confirmed_historical, player_observation, player_hypothesis, selected_not_built, planned_not_built, assistant_recommendation, verified_corpus_fact, unknown, and superseded. Product proposals remain proposals: the suggested first native slice is explicitly a candidate, not a locked MVP.

The dumps have no original prompt timestamps and derive from overlapping conversation branches, so chronology uses only explicit before/after language and is not a fully dated save log. Historical checkpoints do not silently overwrite current unknowns, and current ownership, counts, inventories, progression, construction, and unresolved incidents require live refresh where marked unknown. Repeated statements strengthen provenance but remain one canonical fact; the three raw dumps stay intact, no competing game-data snapshot is created, and replay is idempotent rather than a new promotion.

The canonical outputs are models/rourke-update1-save-baseline__20260711.json for current installed state; models/rourke-update1-play-history__20260711.json (profile rourke-update1-play-history__20260711, as_of 2026-07-11) for historical checkpoints, incidents, and durable preferences; Topics/StarRupture/Player save - play history.md for the human-readable timeline; and Projects/RuptureOps/Player-derived product requirements.md for requirements derived from play evidence without declaring every idea an MVP feature. The earlier ZIP import remains canonical for its screenshots, generated reports, and more complete initial factory-planning transcript.

answer.answer: Little Cloud is modest; Starry Night is even lighter. Bank excess ammunition and consumables if storage is close; otherwise advance carefully, preserving a reserve and recovery cache. Clear Starry Night’s wanderers, take its final chest first, then loot.

claims.value: Little Cloud is about 2/5 difficulty: 13 persistent hostile spawn entries within 250 units—8 tier-1 melee, 4 tier-1 ranged, and 1 tier-1 exploder—with no mapped Goliaths, Flingers, tier-2 enemies, or raid-class concentration. These markers indicate possible population, not simultaneous attackers; the player later completed it and called it “no big deal.”

Bank excess ammunition and consumables first if storage is reasonably close. Otherwise proceed methodically, retain an ammunition/healing reserve, and keep replacement equipment in a separate safe recovery cache; at Starry Night, clear wanderers, open the final chest first, then loot debris.

The tagged nearby Regeneration Chamber reduces return travel but does not protect or replace carried gear. A claimed chamber can go offline if its local base is disabled by corruption, resulting in respawn at the starting launcher; the exact corruption threshold and universal chamber-disable rules remain unverified. Keep replacement weapons, ammunition, healing, and rebuilding materials outside the contested base’s failure domain.

Starry Night is about 1/5 difficulty, with zero persistent hostile spawn markers within 250 units, though roaming enemies can wander in. Its guaranteed final chest contains an Electronics Blueprint, Rotor Blueprint, 15 Armory Tokens, and a Frame Memory Module.

answer.answer: The first Geo Scanner became manageable only after treating it as a staged defense with powered turrets and independent recovery supplies, while retaining uncertainty about both chamber-disable mechanics and loot.

claims.value: The first attempt ended in death; the nearby claimed respawn base lacked spare weapons and replacement materials, forcing a return to Landerworks. On the second attempt, installed but unpowered turrets provided no defense; the player was overwhelmed, corruption disabled the contested base and claimed Regeneration Chamber, and death respawned the player at the starting launcher.

The third attempt succeeded after the player built out the temporary fire base and powered every turret. The automated defense completed the Geo Scanner encounter and changed the experience into a strongly positive payoff.

The two deaths, nonfunctional unpowered turrets, corruption-disabled base and Regeneration Chamber, launcher respawn, and powered-turret success are direct player-reported observations from one encounter. They do not establish a universal corruption threshold or every condition under which a Regeneration Chamber becomes disabled.

For future activations: treat the scanner as a deliberate defense event; claim a nearby Regeneration Chamber but plan for its failure; power and function-check every turret before activation; maintain a separate safe cache with at least one replacement weapon kit, ammunition, healing, and rebuilding materials; and preserve a worst-case route to a stable base or launcher. The reported loot remains unresolved: it may have been two good food-related rewards or stacks and may have involved a quantity of 20, but neither the item identities nor exact counts are verified. The completed scanner and its coordinates also remain unidentified.

answer.answer: The honest MVP is a manually synchronized, versioned iPhone Watch Session: an across-the-room next-event countdown, conservative threat guidance, separately evidenced opportunities, and native alerts that expose their permissions and uncertainty. claims.value: Evidence/version boundary: the corpus is frozen at 2026-07-11. Latest verified public behavior is Early Access Update 1 Hotfix `0.2.8`, Steam build `23761620`, released `2026-06-17`; numerical timer data instead belongs to SRDB `2.3.4`, snapshot `ea-u1-gv35118973__srdb-2.3.4__20260711T050230Z`, captured `2026-07-11T05:02:30.009644Z`, whose source claims Update 1 internal game version `35118973` corresponding contextually—not by an SRDB-published equivalence—to `ea_u1_0.2.0_build_22674441`. The implemented definition is `ruptura-cycle/u1-srdb-2.3.4/r1`, a `3_240_000` ms community/game-data model, not an official invariant. Confidence must be qualitative: `Unsynced`, `Manual sync - predicted`, confirmed at a later transition, `Drift suspected`, or model changed/re-sync required; never invent numeric accuracy. Downgrade after large correction, device-clock or model change, uncertain pause, save/reload, or server stop. Several Hotfix 0.2.8 cycles across solo, hosted co-op, and dedicated-server play remain required before using “exact,” “safe,” or “guaranteed.”
source_paths: Projects/RuptureOps/Rupture cycle timer - research and product design.md

claims.value: Player-facing timeline: preserve the 54-minute engine model but present Fire wave `0:00-0:30` (“Remain sheltered”), Cooling `0:30-1:30` (“Remain sheltered”), Recovery/quiet window `1:30-11:30` (“Lower ambient threat; use the window”), World active `11:30-51:30` (“Ordinary enemies and ecology active”), and Ruptura warning `51:30-54:00` (“Return, bank loot, and shelter”). Manual cycle zero is the local moment the fire wall reaches the player. The portrait hierarchy, entirely above the fold, is: (1) sync/confidence and sound, haptic, notification, loud-alarm, and screen-awake capability; (2) semantic hero state plus a huge monospaced countdown and explicit target; (3) threat instruction and one action; (4) at most two opportunity cards; and (5) exact-time next events plus always-visible `Mute one cycle` and `Re-sync`. The hero counts to the phase’s meaningful event—Cooling beginning during Fire wave, Recovery beginning during Cooling, expected ordinary-Vermin return during Recovery, warning start during World active, and impact during Ruptura warning—not merely elapsed cycle time. Retain a proportional overview rail, but add minimum/equal-width labeled steps or a next-events list so short Burning and Cooling phases remain usable; color must remain secondary to text, symbols, borders, and patterns.
source_paths: Projects/RuptureOps/Rupture cycle timer - research and product design.md

claims.value: Opportunities are independently versioned evidence records, not consequences baked into phase mechanics. Each record needs an ID, start/end event or offset, action, caveat, evidence class, confidence, applicable game build, and source snapshot. The implemented model keeps opportunities in a separate array with ranges, evidence class, confidence, and rank: lower POI threat, Oxallop, caves/Quartz/Glowcaps, Ignitium, eggs, and regrowth are qualified by community-derived/official provenance and caveats; Star Tears are experimental; Sulheart stays hidden until validated. Surface no more than two prioritized cards and say “lower threat,” “expected,” or “favorable,” because triggered Geo Scanner, monolith, infection, Base Core, and scripted POI encounters may persist. Preserve the Ignitium/Star Tears choice rather than claiming both are simultaneously available, and keep enemy return and gathering windows movable independently of source-phase boundaries.
source_paths: Projects/RuptureOps/Rupture cycle timer - research and product design.md

claims.value: Alert/native safety boundary: enemy-return and Ruptura alerts require distinct sounds and haptics, with text and static visual shape so neither color nor audio is the sole signal. Enemy defaults are 5 minutes, 2 minutes, 1 minute, 15 seconds, and expected return; Ruptura offers optional 10 minutes, then 5 minutes, 2:30, 1 minute, 30 seconds, 15 seconds, and impact. Support `Full`, `Haptic only`, and `Visual only`, separate phase/enemy/Ruptura/opportunity toggles, preview, an exit buffer, and `Mute one cycle`. Never replay missed cues after resume or clock correction: reconcile to one current-state message; the implemented planner also treats foreground cues over `5_000` ms late as stale, deduplicates using sync epoch, definition ID, event ID, and cycle index, suppresses paused-session alerts, and mutes through the current cycle’s next impact. Schedule local notifications at absolute dates and replace them after anchor/model/policy changes; show permission/capability and next-alert time. Disable the idle timer only while the monitor is active and restore it afterward; never use background audio as keep-alive. Use a Live Activity only for the currently armed event. AlarmKit is proposed only for an explicitly armed iOS 26 alarm—never an endless automatic 54-minute alarm; earlier systems use normal local notifications, Time Sensitive is opt-in, and Critical Alerts are inappropriate. Avoid flashing red and default per-second ticking; support Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, high contrast, Differentiate Without Color, and Reduce Motion. Included services implement notification replacement, permission reporting, foreground deduplication, distinct double/triple haptics, and idle-timer restoration, but the frozen `2026-07-11T2314Z` checkpoint records no `@main` app, SwiftUI timeline view, successful build/tests, simulator QA, signing, or phone-install handoff, so readiness is unverified.
